body.statement:
There are constants \(u_0=u_0(s,M)\in(0,1]\) and \(C_b=C_b(s,M)<\infty\), and an i.i.d. continuum \(\{Q_u:|u|\le u_0\}\subset\mathcal P_n\), with the following properties.  Every member has cutoff \(c_{Q_u}=c_0\), compliance jump \(d_{Q_u}=\kappa_n\), and causal label \(\theta_{Q_u}=u\).  Conditionally on \(X=x\), its observed \(D\) and \(Y\) are independent Bernoulli variables.  The treatment mean is \((1-\kappa_n)/2\) to the left of \(c_0\) and \((1+\kappa_n)/2\) to the right.  With \(\phi(v)=(1-v^2)_+^2\), \(A_u=\kappa_n|u|\), and a width \(h_u\) proportional to \((A_u/M)^{1/s}\), the outcome means for \(u\ne0\) are
\[
 m_u^-(x)=\frac12-\frac{\kappa_nu}{2}\phi\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h_u}\right),
 \qquad
 m_u^+(x)=\frac12+\frac{\kappa_nu}{2}\phi\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h_u}\right),
\]
on the left and right sides, respectively; for \(u=0\), both means equal \(1/2\).  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le C_b n(\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s},
 \qquad
 \chi^2(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le \exp\!\{C_b n(\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s}\}-1.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\phi(v)=(1-v^2)_+^2\).  On \((-1,1)\),
\[
 \phi'(v)=-4v(1-v^2),\qquad \phi''(v)=-4+12v^2,
\]
whereas \(\phi\) and \(\phi'\) vanish continuously at \(-1\) and \(1\).  Thus \(\phi\) is Lipschitz, \(\phi'\) is globally Lipschitz, and, for every fixed \(s\in[1,2]\), direct rescaling supplies a finite constant \(B_s\ge1\) such that, for \(0<h\le1\) and every scalar \(a\),
\[
 \left\|a\phi\!\left(\frac{\cdot-c_0}{h}\right)\right\|_{\mathcal H^s}
 \le B_s|a|h^{-s}.
\]
For \(s=1\) this follows from the bound on \(\phi'\).  For \(1<s\le2\), writing \(\beta=s-1\), the Lipschitz and boundedness bounds on \(\phi'\) imply \([\phi']_\beta<\infty\), and the displayed scaling follows by the chain rule.  This verifies the required assertion without an external smoothness result.

Set
\[
 u_0=\min\!\left\{1,\frac{4M}{B_s4^s}\right\},
 \qquad
 h_u=\left(\frac{2B_sA_u}{M}\right)^{1/s}
 \quad (u\ne0).
\]
Because \(\kappa_n\le1/8\) and \(|u|\le u_0\),
\[
 h_u^s=\frac{2B_s\kappa_n|u|}{M}
 \le \frac{B_su_0}{4M}
 \le4^{-s},
\]
so \(h_u\le1/4\).  Hence the two observed half-bumps are supported inside \([0,1]\).  Their \(\mathcal H^s\) seminorm contribution is at most
\[
 B_s\frac{A_u}{2}h_u^{-s}=\frac M4.
\]
The constant baseline contributes at most \(1/2\), and \(M\ge2\); consequently each outcome branch has a radius-\(M\) H\"older extension.  The treatment branches are constant and bounded by one, so they also have radius at most \(M\).  All displayed Bernoulli means lie in \([0,1]\), because \(A_u\le1/8\).

We next construct the full-data causal lift.  At \(X=c_0\), assign response-type probabilities
\[
 Q_u(R=A)=Q_u(R=N)=\frac{1-\kappa_n}{2},
 \qquad Q_u(R=C)=\kappa_n,
\]
and define \(D(z)\) from the monotone response type.  For always-takers and never-takers, take a common binary potential outcome under both treatment states, with respective means
\[
 \frac{1-\kappa_nu}{2}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \frac{1+\kappa_nu}{2}.
\]
For compliers, choose binary potential outcomes with means
\[
 E_{Q_u}[Y(0)\mid R=C,X=c_0]=\frac{1-u}{2},
 \qquad
 E_{Q_u}[Y(1)\mid R=C,X=c_0]=\frac{1+u}{2}.
\]
A joint binary pair with these two marginals exists, for example by conditional independence.  Under assignment \(z=0\), the treated units are precisely the always-takers.  Their outcome mean is \((1-\kappa_nu)/2\), and the mean among the untreated never-taker--complier mixture is
\[
 \frac{(1-\kappa_n)(1+\kappa_nu)+2\kappa_n(1-u)}{2(1+\kappa_n)}
 =\frac{1-\kappa_nu}{2}.
\]
Thus \(D(0)\) and \(Y(D(0))\) are independent, and the marginal outcome mean is \((1-\kappa_nu)/2\).  Under assignment \(z=1\), the untreated units are precisely the never-takers, and the analogous treated-mixture calculation is
\[
 \frac{(1-\kappa_n)(1-\kappa_nu)+2\kappa_n(1+u)}{2(1+\kappa_n)}
 =\frac{1+\kappa_nu}{2}.
\]
Hence \(D(1)\) and \(Y(D(1))\) are independent, with marginal outcome mean \((1+\kappa_nu)/2\).

For \(x\ne c_0\), apply to every potential-outcome bit the same type-independent refresh kernel: retain the cutoff bit with probability \(\phi((x-c_0)/h_u)\) and otherwise replace it by an independent fair bit.  On the assigned left side this maps \((1-\kappa_nu)/2\) to \(m_u^-(x)\); on the assigned right side it maps \((1+\kappa_nu)/2\) to \(m_u^+(x)\).  Because the kernel is common across response types, the observed conditional independence of \(D\) and \(Y\) is retained.  Because its retention probability tends to one as \(x\to c_0\), both \(x\mapsto E_{Q_u}[D(z)\mid X=x]\) and \(x\mapsto E_{Q_u}[Y(D(z))\mid X=x]\) are continuous at \(c_0\), for each \(z\).  Take \(X\) uniform on \([0,1]\), set \(Z=\mathbf 1\{X\ge c_0\}\), impose consistency and exclusion, and take independent copies across units.  The cutoff is interior, monotonicity holds by construction, and
\[
 d_{Q_u}=\frac{1+\kappa_n}{2}-\frac{1-\kappa_n}{2}=\kappa_n,
 \qquad
 y_{Q_u}=m_u^+(c_0)-m_u^-(c_0)=\kappa_nu.
\]
Thus the strength shell holds and \(\theta_{Q_u}=y_{Q_u}/d_{Q_u}=u\).  The conditional complier contrast is also directly
\[
 E_{Q_u}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=C,X=c_0]=u.
\]
All member properties in \(\texttt{def:model-class}\) have now been checked, so \(Q_u\in\mathcal P_n\).

It remains to establish the divergences.  Under \(Q_0\), the conditional outcome probability is \(1/2\).  Under \(Q_u\), write it as \(1/2+\delta_u(x)\), where \(|\delta_u(x)|\le A_u/2\).  For \(|\delta|<1/2\), the scalar inequality \(\log(1+v)\le v\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{kl}\!\left(\frac12+\delta,\frac12\right)
 &=\left(\frac12+\delta\right)\log(1+2\delta)
   +\left(\frac12-\delta\right)\log(1-2\delta)\\
 &\le4\delta^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The treatment factors cancel in the likelihood ratio, and uniformity of \(X\), compact support of \(\phi\), and \(0\le\phi\le1\) yield
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_u,Q_0)
 \le A_u^2\int_0^1\phi^2\!\left(\frac{x-c_0}{h_u}\right)dx
 \le2A_u^2h_u.
\]
Additivity under independent sampling therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le 2\left(\frac{2B_s}{M}\right)^{1/s}nA_u^{2+1/s}.
\]
For the chi-square bound, the one-observation likelihood ratio for the outcome factor is \(1+2(2Y-1)\delta_u(X)\).  Consequently
\[
 \chi^2(Q_u,Q_0)=4\int_0^1\delta_u(x)^2dx\le2A_u^2h_u.
\]
Factorization of the squared likelihood ratio under the product law gives
\[
 \chi^2(Q_u^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\{1+\chi^2(Q_u,Q_0)\}^n-1
 \le\exp\!\left\{2\left(\frac{2B_s}{M}\right)^{1/s}nA_u^{2+1/s}\right\}-1.
\]
Taking \(C_b=2(2B_s/M)^{1/s}\) proves both claims.  The case \(u=0\) follows by defining \(Q_0\) with outcome mean identically \(1/2\), in which case both divergences vanish.
